nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are EHDs and what are some examples of them?
nodes.answer: EHDs, or electronic health devices, include items like glucose test strips, smart health patches, hearing aids, drug-releasing pumps, and electronic surgical tools.
nodes.paragraph: treatment) and non-clinical (provision of indi- rect patient care, i.e. hospital administration) services by employing semiconductive elements like transistors and integrated circuits to transform electrical energy into intel- ligent operations such as memory management, gesture control, and remote computing service. EHDs include but are not limited to glucose test strips, smart health patches, hearing aids, drug-releasing pumps, and electronic surgical tools (Shaw et al. 2016). While there are great opportunities created by the use of EHDs, these devices may also place a large burden on the environment. EHDs have both direct and indirect environ- mental impacts. Direct impacts are attributed to the life cycle stages of the device including raw material extraction, manu - facturing, distribution, use, and end-of-life (EOL). Currently, the healthcare sector mainly relies on a linear supply chain composed of single-use electronic devices (Benedettini 2022 ). This inherently unsustainable production and con - sumption model results in the depletion of natural resources, as well as excessive generation of e-waste (MacNeill et al. 2020).
